ed.
Across the pond, more people were getting frustrating working with Ken Thompson's line editor

When Thompson visited
UC Berkeley
in 1976, he brough with him a broken Pascal compiler for UNIX that needed to be fixed.
Bill Joy
, a student from UC Berkeley, was in charge of fixing Thompson's Pascal system. As days passed, Joy noticed that
ed
was holding him back.

vi.
In the summer of 1976, when George Coulouris visited UC Berkeley, he brought a
DECtape
containing
em
and showed it to various people at the university. Some considered this new type of text editor to be a resource hog, while others, including Bill Joy, were impressed with Coulouris' program.

and by their own tweaks to Ken Thompson's

Bill Joy and Chuck Haley (both graduate students at UC Berkeley) created a new editor called

Soon after, they "extended" the

editor and created

. In October of 1977, Bill Joy added a full-screen visual mode to
ex,
which came to be

vi
is basically
ex's visual mode
.

43691020.article_summary: 这篇文章回顾了Vi和Vim文本编辑器的起源与演变，它们的发展与开源软件历史紧密相连。文章提到，Vim的创始人Bram Moolenaar去世，引发了作者对Vim历史的反思。Vim的发展可追溯到1973年，英国首个UNIX系统安装在伦敦玛丽女王大学，George Coulouris教授在那里开发了名为"em"的编辑器，推动了"vi"及其他"vi克隆"的诞生。早期UNIX的"ed"编辑器因适用于电传打字机而设计，但随着显示终端普及，其单行编辑模式显得不便。Coulouris改进了"ed”创造出"em"，而UC Berkeley的Bill Joy受其启发，开发出全屏模式的"vi"编辑器。最终，"vi"从"ex"编辑器的可视模式演变而来，成为广泛使用的文本编辑器。

主要讨论点：围绕文本编辑器（尤其是Vi及其衍生工具）的历史、设计、功能及其现代应用的讨论。

不同观点：
• **Vi的历史和技术影响**：[bsenftner]分享了在哈佛大学学习汇编语言课程的经历，通过实现一个迷你版Vi来掌握汇编语言的技能。这体现了Vi在早期计算机教育中的重要性及其技术深度。
• **Vi设计的优越性**：[qsort]认为Vi设计精良，即使其简化版（如Busybox中的Vi）也比现代IDE更强大，表达了对Vi及其设计理念的强烈支持。
• **TECO作为早期编辑器的影响**：[CalChris]提出TECO可能是Vi等编辑器的早期原型，尽管没有直接证据表明TECO对Vi的影响，但其时间线上的先导地位值得注意。
• **Vim的学习与应用**：[nickandbro]正在开发Vimgolf.ai项目，旨在让学习Vim的过程更加有趣，并逐步引入不同的操作动作，强调了Vim在现代编程学习中的应用潜力。

补充讨论：
• **Minix编辑器的演变**：[bodyfour]指出Minix在2013年将默认编辑器从Elvis切换到BSD nvi，并提到Minix在2018年后没有新的提交，这为讨论Vi及其衍生版本在不同操作系统中的应用提供了背景。
• **Vi在现代技术环境中的持久性**：[sunshine-o]认为Vi和UNIX shell是美丽的工具，即使在现代技术环境中仍然具有生命力，并预测Vi在未来50年可能仍有用户，显示了对Vi持久价值的信心。
• **其他早期编辑器的提及**：[kjellsbells]提到MS-DOS中的EDLIN与UNIX ed的相似性，[Animats]指出RAND编辑器是所有全屏终端编辑器的祖先，[jasperry]提到Vim的第一个版本是为Amiga开发的，[jiehong]和[drbig]则分别对ADM-3A设计和CygnusED进行了评论。

争议焦点：

这些观点共同勾勒出Vi及其相关工具在计算机历史中的重要性，以及其在现代编程环境中的持续影响和应用潜力。

data.article_summary: 这篇文章简要介绍了椭圆曲线的基本概念及其在密码学中的应用。椭圆曲线由特定方程定义，其图形呈光滑的环状曲线。它们在密码学中被用于创建数字签名和加密数据，尤其常见于椭圆曲线密码学（ECC）。ECC基于椭圆曲线离散对数问题（ECDLP），该问题极难解决，从而确保了数据的安全性。与传统方法如RSA相比，椭圆曲线更高效，能在提供同等安全性的情况下使用更小的密钥尺寸，因此在如TLS和比特币等系统中广泛应用。椭圆曲线不仅是流行术语，更是确保数字世界安全的重要数学工具。

What the hell is an elliptic curve?
April 20, 2025

TheCommieAxolotl
Founder, OnlyNv
Have you ever been browsing the web and come across a term that made you go, "
huh?
" Well, if you're even slightly cryptographcally inclined, you might have stumbled upon the term
elliptic curve
and thought to yourself, "
What the hell?
" Don't worry, you're not alone in feeling a bit lost.
An elliptic curve is a type of mathematical function that has some pretty cool properties. It's defined by a specific equation, usually in the form of

These curves have a unique feature: they can be used to create a group of points that can be added together in a unique way to form new points. This is what makes them so useful in cryptography.

Elliptic curves are commonly used in cryptographic algorithms, like computing digital signatures or encrypting data. The most common use is in
Elliptic Curve Cryptography
, which is a form of public-key cryptography that uses the mathematics of elliptic curves to secure data.
The fundamental algorithm behind ECC is based on the
Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem
. This problem is extremely hard to solve, which means that it's difficult for an adversary to brute-force the encryption. In simple terms, if you have a point on the curve and you know how to combine points together, it's easy to find the result. But if you only have the result and one of the points, it's really hard to figure out the other point.

Elliptic curves are also more efficient than traditional cryptographic methods like
RSA
. They can provide the same level of security with smaller key sizes, which means faster computations and less complexity. This is especially important for a world with increasingly more devices with limited processing power, like smartphones and IoT devices.
This efficiency is one of the reasons why elliptic curves have become so popular in modern cryptography. They are widely used in everyday systems, like
TLS
(Transport Layer Security), which secures your web browsing, and in cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum, which use elliptic curves to secure transactions and wallets.
So, next time you see the term elliptic curve, feel free to picture the graphics above and remember that it's not just a buzzword. It's a powerful mathematical tool that plays a crucial role in keeping your data safe and secure in the digital world.

data.title: Attention Spans for Math and Stories (2019)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过故事激发儿童对数学的兴趣，尤其是对年幼儿童而言。文章提到在一个MathOverflow讨论中，人们探讨了适合5-6岁儿童的数学游戏，强调了成年人往往低估5岁儿童的理解能力。对于年幼的孩子，抽象逻辑游戏的吸引力在于提出核心玩法之外的问题，比如Set游戏中的特殊技巧，但这些通常要到7-8岁后才会引发兴趣。文章指出，通过故事引导孩子学习数学概念非常有效，例如通过《The Boy Who Loved Math》这本书，作者成功地让一个5岁的小女孩Anna对质数产生了兴趣，尽管她之前对数学并无特别关注。作者还分享了自己作为夏令营辅导员通过编造秘密特工训练故事吸引孩子们注意力的经验，强调了故事讲述在教育中的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过故事和情境帮助理解数学和设计

不同观点：
• vonnik: 认为建筑和设计中的每个物体都蕴含着一个故事，这些故事不仅体现在物体内部各部分的关系上，还体现在这些部分与外部世界（如使用者）的关系上。通过观察六岁孩子用乐高积木构建并解释每个部分的功能，他意识到设计的本质就是在讲故事，且这些故事会随着人们的需求和期望改变而变化。

• aoki: 主张在基础数学和本科数学之间需要更多以故事为导向的内容，类似于YouTube频道Numberphile中的某些节目。建议通过故事引入更深的理论，同时保持趣味性，并提到Beast Academy漫画系列是一个不错的儿童数学启蒙资源。

• AudiomaticApp: 提起Murderous Maths（一本以故事形式讲解数学的书），可能是在回应aoki的观点，暗示这类书籍可以作为数学教育的补充材料。

• ho_schi: 对通过故事来进行数学教育的方法表示赞同，但带有个人感慨，认为这种方法在自身童年时未被采用，是一种遗憾。

• wslh: 分享了Raymond Smullyan的书中提到的故事，强调通过故事激发逻辑和数学兴趣的有效性，并提到一个孩子虽然喜欢解谜却不被告知这是数学，因为他讨厌数学，这暗示了故事在克服对数学反感方面的潜在作用。

• sinenomine: 从遗传学和统计学角度提出不同观点，认为数学能力和智力的遗传性导致天才数学家的孩子往往不如父母，并认为早期教育计划难以弥补这种差距。这与其他人强调教育方法的观点形成对比。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个具体资源和例子，如John Collison的推文、Numberphile、Beast Academy、Murderous Maths和Raymond Smullyan的书，这些都被视为通过故事促进数学理解的有效工具。
• sinenomine的观点引发了对天赋和遗传限制的讨论，与其他评论中强调教育方法的乐观态度形成对比，成为争议的焦点。
• 总体而言，讨论围绕如何通过故事和情境更好地理解和教授数学和设计，但也有对个体差异和遗传因素的现实考虑。

Attention spans for math and stories
#essays
2024-11-15
Editor’s note
: This essay was originally published in 2019.
I have made minor edits in this republishing.
There was a
MathOverflow
thread
about mathematically interesting games for 5–6 year olds. A lot of the
discussion revolved around how young age 5 really is, and how we should temper
expectations because we don’t really remember what it’s like to be 5. In
response to an
enormous answer
by
Alexander Chervov, user LSpice quipped, “‘Daddy, daddy, let’s play another in
the infinite indexed family of perfect-information draw-free cheap-to-construct
two-player games!’” That being said,
Martín-Blas Pérez Pinilla’s “sprouts”
game
piqued my interest to find
optimal strategies.
Most abstract logic games that are interesting to mathy folks are only
interesting when you start asking questions beyond core gameplay. For example,
the game
Set
is interesting when you ask, “how
many cards can you have with no set?” or similar
tricks to determine the last
un-dealt card
in a
deck just by viewing the remaining board. These have little to do with skill at
playing the game.
I’ve found that children under a certain age,
maybe 7 or 8,
haven’t learned how to be curious about such questions yet.
They like
knowing
things and
experiencing
things.
They enjoy surprising patterns
or natural phenomena (like vinegar and baking soda),
but still aren’t really
curious
enough about them to
be persistent in studying them.
For children to exercise mathematical reasoning skills, and for teachers and
parents to get the opportunity to teach curiousity and persistence, they have
to be motivated. People with an eye for science, people who in their adulthood
marvel at the splendor of nature, often neglect that at age 5, there is one
simple thing that kids embrace with all their being, justification-free, which
can be used as a vessel for abstract reasoning: storytelling. Be good at
storytelling.
A few years ago, my cousin’s daughter was 5 years old. I’ll refer to her as
Anna. Anna is of Hungarian descent, lives in Germany, and speaks functional
English. My cousin knew her daughter was bright, but she was at a loss for what
to give Anna to occupy her mind. So naturally I sent my cousin the book, “
The
Boy Who Loved
Math
.”
Cover of
The Boy Who Loved Math
It’s a story about Paul Erdős, the famous Hungarian mathematician. The book is
in English, about a Hungarian boy, and involves a strict German nanny.
Naturally, Anna loved the book because she had someone to identify with her
multiplex identity.
At its most mathematical, “The Boy Who Loved Math” explains what a prime number
is, and Anna learned it immediately. My cousin told me about how one day they
were listening to the radio in the car, and a game show was playing where the
prize-winning question was (I paraphrase), “What is the name for a number that
has only itself and 1 as a factor?” The contestant on the radio couldn’t
answer, but Anna pipes up, “That’s easy, it’s a prime!” To the best of my
knowledge, she had no interest in math before this, and she had no use for
knowing what a prime number is. But simply having the idea
of a prime number wrapped up in a story about someone like her was enough to
pique her interest.
This story has nothing to do with math, but has a lot to do with storytelling.
I worked as a day camp counselor for a few summers in high school and college.
My main age group was 5-6 year old boys and girls. It’s a lovely age group
because they’re old enough to understand complex ideas, but too young to
directly challenge you when you lie to them. And I lied like the wind.
My shtick was to tell the kids that the summer camp was a secret agent training
camp. All the counselors were former secret agents that had retired and were
now training the next generation. By the end of each 3-week session, most of
the kids figured out that it was make-believe, but it was
fun
make-believe
and there was just enough to keep it plausible.
The crown jewel of this act was that it was an infinite time sink. Often
enough, our schedule had us playing an hour of field hockey followed by an hour
of tennis in 95 degree heat (even in normal weather, a 6 year old won’t have
more than 15 minutes of tennis in them before they get bored or frustrated by a
lack of hand-eye coordination). On such hot days, I would end the activities
early and have the kids gather around in the shade to regale them with a tale
about a “mission” another counselor and I had embarked on in our long, storied
career.
The formula was pretty simple:
Pick an evil boss: Doctor Euler.
Choose an exotic locale for a base: inside an iceberg.
Pick an “element” (sand, grass, dirt, mud) for the evil boss’s henchmen to
be built out of (so that we can “kill” them without resorting to gratuitous
violence; guns don’t work on grass monsters).
As you can tell from the name of the evil boss, I liked to slip in math names

43709843.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过故事激发儿童对数学的兴趣，尤其是对年幼儿童而言。文章提到在一个MathOverflow讨论中，人们探讨了适合5-6岁儿童的数学游戏，强调了成年人往往低估5岁儿童的理解能力。对于年幼的孩子，抽象逻辑游戏的吸引力在于提出核心玩法之外的问题，比如Set游戏中的特殊技巧，但这些通常要到7-8岁后才会引发兴趣。文章指出，通过故事引导孩子学习数学概念非常有效，例如通过《The Boy Who Loved Math》这本书，作者成功地让一个5岁的小女孩Anna对质数产生了兴趣，尽管她之前对数学并无特别关注。作者还分享了自己作为夏令营辅导员通过编造秘密特工训练故事吸引孩子们注意力的经验，强调了故事讲述在教育中的重要性。
43709843.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过故事和情境帮助理解数学和设计

不同观点：
• vonnik: 认为建筑和设计中的每个物体都蕴含着一个故事，这些故事不仅体现在物体内部各部分的关系上，还体现在这些部分与外部世界（如使用者）的关系上。通过观察六岁孩子用乐高积木构建并解释每个部分的功能，他意识到设计的本质就是在讲故事，且这些故事会随着人们的需求和期望改变而变化。

• aoki: 主张在基础数学和本科数学之间需要更多以故事为导向的内容，类似于YouTube频道Numberphile中的某些节目。建议通过故事引入更深的理论，同时保持趣味性，并提到Beast Academy漫画系列是一个不错的儿童数学启蒙资源。

• AudiomaticApp: 提起Murderous Maths（一本以故事形式讲解数学的书），可能是在回应aoki的观点，暗示这类书籍可以作为数学教育的补充材料。

• ho_schi: 对通过故事来进行数学教育的方法表示赞同，但带有个人感慨，认为这种方法在自身童年时未被采用，是一种遗憾。

• wslh: 分享了Raymond Smullyan的书中提到的故事，强调通过故事激发逻辑和数学兴趣的有效性，并提到一个孩子虽然喜欢解谜却不被告知这是数学，因为他讨厌数学，这暗示了故事在克服对数学反感方面的潜在作用。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及到多个具体资源和例子，如John Collison的推文、Numberphile、Beast Academy、Murderous Maths和Raymond Smullyan的书，这些都被视为通过故事促进数学理解的有效工具。
• sinenomine的观点引发了对天赋和遗传限制的讨论，与其他评论中强调教育方法的乐观态度形成对比，成为争议的焦点。
• 总体而言，讨论围绕如何通过故事和情境更好地理解和教授数学和设计，但也有对个体差异和遗传因素的现实考虑。

data.article_summary: lit.money是一款专注于简化个人财务管理的新应用，目前处于测试阶段，已有190多名用户加入。该应用旨在通过自动标记收入与支出、清晰的现金流展示、以及安全地与家人或团队共享财务信息等功能，提供简单、私密且安全的用户体验。它强调数据隐私，承诺不会出售用户数据，并采用高级加密方法保护财务信息。测试阶段免费，未来定价将保持公平和简约。用户可以随时删除自己的数据，并直接联系开发者反馈问题或提出建议。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人理财网络应用的开发和数据隐私保护

不同观点：
• [trollbridge] 认为许多云服务承诺不卖用户数据，但很难真正做到。他正在开发一个软件，确保其能够在本地或用户自选的云基础设施上运行，以兑现这一承诺。他选择了AGPL3许可协议，以避免第三方托管平台对用户进行锁定。同时，他也提到某些服务（如Plaid）在自托管时几乎无法使用，但他们找到了替代方案。

• [djfobbz] 提到大约18年前有一个类似的网站被推出，引用了Hacker News上的历史讨论链接，暗示类似的想法或项目可能已经存在，对新项目的独特性提出质疑。

• [nimishpatel19] 支持[mhrnik]的项目，表示该应用简化了他的个人理财，并成功与他的会计分享了数据，给予项目良好祝愿。

• [mhrnik] 分享了他创建lit.Money的背景和动机，强调了他对现有应用的不满，尤其是在UI设计和数据分享功能上的不足。他详细介绍了lit.Money的关键功能，包括数据集中查看、一键删除数据、自定义权限的财务分享空间（Finspace）以及批量编辑和数据导出功能。他还提供了DEMO模式和视频演示链接，寻求社区反馈。

补充讨论：
• [mhrnik] 强调lit.Money的开发初衷是为了满足个人需求，而非追求成为“下一个大事物”，反映出一种务实、用户导向的开发理念。

争议焦点：
• [djfobbz] 对新项目的独特性提出质疑，指出类似项目早在18年前就已存在，暗示可能存在重复发明的问题。

• [trollbridge] 对数据隐私和第三方托管的潜在问题表示关注，提出了自托管和开源许可协议（AGPL3）作为解决方案，但承认某些服务在自托管时存在技术挑战。

总体来看，讨论围绕个人理财应用的功能、数据隐私保护以及项目独特性展开，反映了用户对隐私保护的重视以及对应用功能的具体需求。

data.title: Police algorithm said Lina was at 'medium' risk. Then she was killed
data.author: mmarian
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了西班牙一名叫Lina的女性在其前伴侣的暴力威胁下，尽管向警方求助并被录入VioGén系统评估为“中等”风险，但仍未获得足够保护，最终被前伴侣杀害的悲剧。VioGén是西班牙警方使用的一种算法工具，用于评估家暴受害者再次遭受攻击的风险，并据此分配警力资源。Lina曾请求法院对其前伴侣下达限制令，但被拒绝。她的死亡引发了对VioGén系统有效性的质疑，尤其是中等风险级别的受害者未能得到及时保护。批评者认为，警方过度依赖算法决策，可能忽略了人的判断。尽管警方认为VioGén总体有效，但Lina的案例表明该系统并非万无一失。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：算法责任与事故责任归属的争论

不同观点：
• SOLAR_FIELDS认为，算法本身不应被指责，真正应该负责的是设计和实现算法的个人或组织。他强调，新闻标题不应将责任归咎于模糊的“算法”，而应明确指出是“由X编写并由Y部署的警察软件导致了死亡”。他将责任归结于具体的人为因素，而不是技术本身。

• LatteLazy则从风险评估的角度出发，认为算法所做的只是统计学上的风险预测，类似于购买彩票的中奖概率。尽管有人可能会因为“中等风险”而遭遇不幸，但这只是统计结果与现实的交汇，而非系统性的错误或人为过失。

• rayiner的观点集中在文章中对事件描述的被动语态上。他强烈反对将事件描述为由抽象的“算法”导致的，并指出这是对责任的模糊化处理。他明确指出，真正导致悲剧发生的是人的行为（例如某人故意纵火），而不是技术本身。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于责任归属问题。SOLAR_FIELDS和rayiner都强调个人或组织的责任，而LatteLazy则试图从统计学和风险管理的角度来解释事件，认为这是概率问题，而非直接的人为错误。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对语言和叙述方式的关注，尤其是rayiner对被动语态的批评，认为这种叙述模糊了真正的责任人。
- 三种观点都试图将责任从“算法”这个抽象概念转移到具体的人或机制上，显示出对技术中立性的不同理解。

43742515.article_content:
Image source,
Family handout
Image caption,
Lina died at her home on 9th February, 2025
Linda Pressly and Esperanza Escribano
BBC News
Published
19 April 2025
In January, Lina went to the police.
Her ex-partner had been threatening her at home in the Spanish seaside town of BenalmÃ¡dena. That day, he'd allegedly raised his hand as if to hit her.
"There had been violent episodes - she was scared," Lina's cousin Daniel recalls.
When she got to the police station, she was interviewed and her case registered with VioGÃ©n, a digital tool which assesses the likelihood of a woman being attacked again by the same man.
VioGÃ©n - an algorithm-based system - asks 35 questions about the abuse and its intensity, the aggressor's access to weapons, his mental health and whether the woman has left, or is considering leaving, the relationship.
It then records the threat to her as "negligible", "low", "medium", "high" or "extreme".
The category is used to make decisions about the allocation of police resources to protect the woman.
Lina was deemed to be at "medium" risk.
She asked for a restraining order at a specialist gender violence court in Malaga, so that her ex-partner couldn't be in contact with her or share her living space.  The request was denied.
Can an algorithm predict murder?
Spanish police use an algorithm to assess the risk of repeat domestic violence.  Does it work?
Listen on Sounds
"Lina wanted to change the locks at her home, so she could live peacefully with her children," says her cousin.
Three weeks later, she was dead. Her partner had allegedly used his key to enter her flat and soon the house was on fire.
While her children, mother and ex-partner all escaped, Lina didn't. Her 11-year-old son was widely reported as telling police it was his father who killed his mother.
Lina's lifeless body was retrieved from the charred interior of her home. Her ex-partner, the father of her three youngest children, was arrested.
Now, her death is raising questions about VioGÃ©n and its ability to keep women safe in Spain.
Image caption,
Lina's home after the fire
VioGÃ©n didn't accurately predict the threat to Lina.
As a woman designated at "medium" risk, the protocol is that she would be followed up again by a nominated police officer within 30 days.
But Lina was dead before that. If she had been "high" risk, the police follow-up would have happened within a week.  Could that have made a difference to Lina?
Tools to evaluate the threat of repeat domestic violence are used in North America and across Europe. In the UK, some police forces use DARA (Domestic Abuse Risk Assessment) - essentially a checklist. And DASH (Domestic Abuse, Stalking, Harassment and Honour-based Violence Assessment) may be employed by police or others, like social workers, to assess the risk of another attack.
But only in Spain is an algorithm woven so tightly into police practice. VioGÃ©n was developed by Spanish police and academics.  It's used everywhere apart from the Basque Country and Catalonia (those regions have separate systems, although police co-operation is nationwide).
Image caption,
Ch Insp Isabel Espejo believes VioGÃ©n is an invaluable tool
The head of the National Police's family and women's unit in Malaga, Ch Insp Isabel Espejo, describes VioGÃ©n as "super-important".
"It helps us follow each victim's case very precisely," she says.
Her officers deal with an average of 10 reports of gender violence a day. And every month, VioGÃ©n classifies nine or 10 women as being at "extreme" risk of repeat victimisation.
The resource implications in those cases are huge: 24-hour police protection for a woman until the circumstances change and the risk decreases. Women assessed as "high" risk may also get an officer escort.
A 2014 study found that officers accepted VioGÃ©n's evaluation of the likelihood of repeated abuse 95% of the time. Critics suggest police are abdicating decision-making about women's safety to an algorithm.
Ch Insp Espejo says that the algorithm's calculation of risk is usually adequate. But she recognises  - even though Lina's case wasn't under her command - that something went wrong with Lina's assessment.
"I'm not going to say VioGÃ©n doesn't fail â it does. But this wasn't the trigger that led to this woman's murder. The only guilty party is the person who killed Lina. Total security just doesn't exist," she says.
But at "medium" risk, Lina was never a police priority. And did Lina's VioGÃ©n assessment have an impact on the court's decision to deny her a restraining order against her ex-partner?
Image caption,
Judge Maria del Carmen GutiÃ©rrez sits in Malaga's gender violence court
Court authorities didn't give us permission to meet the judge who denied Lina an injunction against her ex-partner - a woman attacked on social media after Lina's death.
Instead, another of Malaga's gender violence judges, Maria del Carmen GutiÃ©rrez tells us in general terms that such an order needs two things: evidence of a crime and

• rayiner的观点集中在文章中对事件描述的被动语态上。他强烈反对将事件描述为由抽象的“算法”导致的，并指出这是对责任的模糊化处理。他明确指出，真正导致悲剧发生的是人的行为（例如某人故意纵火），而不是技术本身。

data.title: AI-generated videos now possible with gaming GPUs with just 6GB of VRAM
data.article_summary: GitHub和斯坦福大学合作推出了FramePack，这是一种新的视频扩散模型架构，通过固定长度的时间上下文处理数据，能够在仅有6GB显存的情况下生成60秒的高质量视频。FramePack通过多阶段优化技术和压缩输入帧来减少GPU内存占用，同时缓解了视频长度增加导致的质量下降问题。该架构适用于现代RTX 30/40/50系列GPU，支持Linux系统，使得AI视频生成更加高效且易于访问。尽管当前模型帧率限制在30 FPS，但它为普通用户提供了制作AI视频的便捷途径。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43742608.article_content:
(Image credit:
GitHub
)
Lvmin Zhang at
GitHub
, in collaboration with Maneesh Agrawala at Stanford University, has introduced FramePack this week. FramePack offers a practical implementation of video diffusion using fixed-length temporal context for more efficient processing, enabling longer and higher-quality videos. A 13-billion parameter model built using the FramePack architecture can generate a 60-second clip with just 6GB of video memory.
FramePack is a neural network architecture that uses multi-stage optimization techniques to enable local AI video generation. At the time of writing, the FramePack GUI is said to run a custom Hunyuan-based model under the hood, though the research paper mentions that existing pre-trained models can be fine-tuned using FramePack.
Typical diffusion models process data from previously generated noisy frames to predict the next, slightly less noisy frame. The number of input frames considered for each prediction is called the temporal context length, which grows with the video size. Standard video diffusion models demand a large VRAM pool, with 12GB being a common starting point. Sure, you can get away with less memory, but that comes at the cost of shorter clips, lower quality, and longer processing times.
You may like
AMD-optimized Stable Diffusion models achieve up to 3.3x performance boost on Ryzen and Radeon
You can now play a real-time AI-rendered Quake II in your browser — Microsoft's WHAMM offers generative AI for games
Enter FramePack: a new architecture that compresses input frames, based on their importance, into a fixed-size context length, drastically reducing GPU memory overhead. All frames must be compressed to converge at a desired upper bound for the context length. The authors describe the computational costs as similar to image diffusion.
(Image credit:
GitHub
)
Coupled with techniques to mitigate "drifting", where the quality degrades with the video's length, FramePack offers longer video generation without significant compromise to fidelity. As it stands, FramePack requires an RTX 30/40/50 series GPU with support for the FP16 and BF16 data formats. Support on Turing and older architectures has not been verified, with no mention of AMD/Intel hardware. Linux is also among the supported Operating Systems.
Aside from the
RTX 3050 4GB
, most modern (RTX) GPUs meet or exceed the 6GB criteria. In terms of speed, an
RTX 4090
can dish out as many as 0.6 frames/second (optimized with teacache), so your mileage will vary depending on your graphics card. Either way, each frame will be displayed after it is generated, providing immediate visual feedback.
The employed model likely has a 30 FPS cap, which might be limiting for many users. That said, instead of relying on costly third-party services, FramePack is paving the way to make AI video generation more accessible for the average consumer. Even if you're not a content creator, this is an entertaining tool for making GIFs, memes, and whatnot. I know I'll be giving it a go in my free time.

data.title: A Map of British Dialects (2023)
data.author: gregorvand
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者绘制的一张详细但不完美的英国方言地图。由于语言的复杂性和演变，方言在地理上存在巨大差异，特别是在英国这样有1600年语言历史的地区。作者花费多年时间，收集研究资料并征求反馈，制作了可能是迄今最详细的方言地图。然而，由于方言的定义和边界模糊，地图永远无法完全准确。方言之间的差异往往是渐变的，而不是截然分开的，因此地图使用虚线表示模糊的边界，并通过颜色渐变展示方言间的相似性。此外，像伦敦这样的大城市方言多样性极高，无法在地图上精确呈现。最终，这张地图尽管详尽，但始终是不完整和不完全准确的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国及其他地区口音和方言的多样性与变化

不同观点：
• PaulRobinson认为，英国的方言和口音变化非常复杂且不断演变，每20英里左右就会发生变化。他提到自己带有“南潘宁”混合口音，并指出这种变化不仅限于英国，其他国家如加拿大和美国也经历了类似的口音变化。他质疑未来英语在几百年后会变成什么样。
• b800h质疑方言地图的时效性，指出埃塞克斯口音在20世纪70年代已经进入赫特福德郡，而考克尼口音已经消失。他还提到现代肯特郡的口音可能是现代河口英语、多元文化伦敦英语和标准发音的混合。
• SeanLuke将英国的方言多样性与意大利的方言情况进行比较，指出意大利有大量不同的方言，这些方言在19世纪中期之前是完全不同的语言。他提到美国和英国对某些词汇的不同称呼源自意大利不同方言，并强调意大利是欧洲方言最密集的地区之一。

• amiga386提到阿伯丁的 Doric 方言，并纠正其他人对方言的错误描述。
• fy20分享了自己在英国西南部靠近县界处听不懂当地人说话的经历，强调口音和方言的显著差异。

• _fw认为西北英格兰，如威根和默西赛德地区的口音有显著差异，并提到不同地方的独特发音。

• pyb提到法国并没有像英国或德国那样强的地域口音。
• zeristor以幽默的方式描述了“Corbyite”这种口音。

补充讨论：
- 英国口音和方言的复杂性和变化性，以及历史和社会因素（如阶级、移民、媒体）对方言的影响。
- 不同地区方言和口音的显著差异，以及这些差异如何影响人们的交流和身份认同。

43734953.article_content:
This map took me a long time to make, and is very detailed, but will always be incomplete and inaccurate due to the nature of language.
Why this map is so detailed
The diversity of English dialects in the United Kingdom is enormous.
It’s common for people from either side of a river, mountain, or even town to speak noticeably different ways, with particular features that immediately mark someone out as being from a specific area, to those who have an ear for it.
This is pretty normal in any large region that has been speaking a language continually for 1600 years. You will find the same thing in Germany, Norway, France, and countless other countries. Languages evolve over time, and physical distance between regions means that new features often spread slowly, leading to dialectal differences. Sometimes these differences are small, and only easily recognised by people from the relevant region. Other times there are very clear distinctions, with neighbouring dialects sounding almost like different languages to those unaccustomed to them.
Here I have tried to capture as much nuance as possible. I’ve spent the last few years pooling together every study, survey, map, and database I can find, and then subjecting my image to several rounds of peer feedback. The members of my Facebook group, “Ah yes, the British accent”, were also a huge help in trying to make these borders as accurate as possible.  The end result is an image which is, to my knowledge, the most detailed map of British dialects ever made. But it is still very much unfinished, and it always will be.
Why this map is wrong, and always will be
Maps are great. They allow us to display complex geographic data in a way that is visually appealing and easily understood. But often reality is just not that simple.
There’s no precise definition of a “dialect”
The definition is easy enough: a dialect is a form of language that has distinct vocabulary, pronunciation (accent), and/or grammar. But how different does a way of speaking need to be to constitute a different dialect? If any noticeable difference between the way two areas speak is a dialect, then my image is actually using very broad categories and missing much detail. My own tiny hometown (on the border between “North Cumbrian” and “West Northumbrian”) has words and pronunciations that don’t fit it into either grouping, but I think showing my town as a distinct bubble here would be a dangerous precedent. During my research for this image I talked with many people who, like me, perceive their village, town, or even street as being distinct from the surrounding area, and they’re probably right. But that kind of precision would make my image far more complicated, far harder to create, and likely far less accurate in other ways. So I’ve drawn lines around larger areas where more obvious distinctions can be found, without any strong criteria for what constitutes a dialect. I’ve also tried to show the similarities between neighbouring dialects by using a colour scheme that changes gradually across the country.
Borders between dialects are rarely hard lines
More often than not, dialects do not suddenly change as you move from one region to another. They flow and merge over time in complex and messy ways, like coloured inks diffusing into water. Yes, there is definitely a difference between the dialect of Barrow in southern Cumbria and Carlisle in the north, but in reality the region between them is a spectrum, and the placement of any dialect border across Cumbria is pretty arbitrary. Dialects on either side of it will have more in common with each other than they do with the rest of their side of the county.
In an attempt to show this, the first few drafts of this map had no white borders, instead just similar neighbouring colours against each other. However, this turned out to be a nightmare for colour-blind people. I then put in a combination of dotted lines for smaller distinctions, and solid, thick lines to show different dialect groups. But that didn’t feel right either, as while it’s easy to group together the East Midlands as separate from the West Midlands, the “Mid” Midlands doesn’t really have any solid distinction like that: it’s a gradient between the two sides. So I’ve left it all as dotted lines, almost as an apology for the map’s inability to show the true messy gradient that exists. I hope they serve to convey the vagueness and permeability of these “borders”.
In reality these colours should blur and fade together with gradients and checkerboard markings and about 35 extra spatial dimensions, but that would very much defeat the point of trying to make an intelligible map.
Some dialects are not geographically specific at all
While most dialects can be described as regional, spoken mainly in one area, that isn’t always the case. London is the prime example of this: my map cops out with “London Dialects” (plural), because in reality London is incredibly diverse, and deserves its own map to show

data.title: Hydrogen vs. Battery Buses: A European Transit Reality Check
data.author: xbmcuser
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了欧洲两个氢能公交车试点项目的失败案例，分别位于布鲁塞尔和苏格兰的阿伯丁。布鲁塞尔的STIB-MIV公交公司结束了氢能公交试验，决定专注于电动公交，主要由于氢燃料的供应不稳定、成本高昂以及基础设施复杂。阿伯丁曾大力推广氢能双层公交，但同样面临燃料成本过高和供应不足的问题，导致车队自2024年7月起停运。相比之下，德国的科隆在氢能公交方面取得了一些成功，得益于来自化工行业的副产品氢气支持以及政府的大量补贴。总体来看，氢能在实际应用中仍面临诸多挑战，而电动公交则被认为更具可行性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：电动巴士与氢能巴士的比较

不同观点：
• **电动巴士胜出**：
  - **[rsynnott]** 认为电动巴士（BEV）已经明显胜出，因为已有大量BEV巴士车队，而氢能巴士车队规模较小。
  - **[m4rtink]** 指出，氢能巴士需要全新基础设施，且保留了化石燃料车辆的缺点（如空气过滤），而电动巴士只需升级变压器和电线，或采用无轨电车结合电池的方案。
  - **[amsha]** 引用“氢能阶梯”图表，认为氢能几乎在所有应用场景中都不如其他清洁技术，尤其是电动技术。
  - **[PaulKeeble]** 强调氢能的整体效率低（约30%），而电池直接供电效率接近100%，因此运营成本更高。
  - **[occz]** 支持无轨电车优于电动巴士和氢能巴士。
  - **[vrighter]** 简单指出，用电力直接给汽车充电比通过氢能转化损失更少。
  
• **氢能有潜在优势**：
  - **[vegavis]** 认为氢能在大型车辆（如矿山车辆、半挂车等）上有优势，因为电池技术无法支持高负载需求，且氢能加注速度更快。尽管目前氢能供应链和投资不足，但未来在工业和物流领域有潜力。

• **其他替代能源**：
  - **[j_4]** 指出电动巴士重量大，可能加速道路损坏，带来额外维护成本。
  - **[fifilura]** 提到生物气（甲烷）巴士作为另一种替代能源，已在许多地方运行，但在讨论中未被提及。

• **现实中的选择**：
  - **[sschueller]** 分享苏黎世交通公司评估后选择电动巴士，尽管目前电池容量只能运行半天，但随着容量提升，这并不影响运营。
  - **[londons_explore]** 分析城市巴士的低速运行特点，认为通过减少滚动阻力、采用热泵和双层玻璃等技术，电动巴士的电池需求可以接近电动汽车，从而降低能源成本。

• **氢能的争议**：

争议焦点：氢能是否应在公共交通中广泛应用，特别是在巴士领域，以及其与电动巴士在成本、效率、基础设施方面的比较。

Two more hydrogen bus trial failures crossed my screen this morning, so I thought I’d share. Both are in Europe, but while one is in the capital of the EU, the other is across the Channel in the heart of the United Kingdom’s oil and gas industry. While I’m at it, I’ll provide a rundown on where all of the EU’s funding has gone, and what the constant refrains are.
Hydrogen Bus Deployments in JIVE (2021–2025) – number of buses, suppliers, hydrogen sourcing, and status.
The News
Lets start with
Brussels
‘ transit agency, STIB-MIV, which just announced that they would not pursue any hydrogen buses after ending the hydrogen trial. Instead, they would focus on battery-electric buses, while not ruling out hydrogen buses in the future, should reality warp and hydrogen become cheap and practical.
Brussels launched its hydrogen bus trial in 2021 with a single Van Hool A330 fuel cell bus, backed by EU funding through the JIVE program. The vehicle was leased for a two-year evaluation period, with the intention of assessing operational performance and environmental benefits relative to other low-emission technologies in STIB’s fleet. The trial included plans to run the bus using green hydrogen, aligning with the city’s broader decarbonization goals.
From a technical standpoint, the bus met expectations. It offered acceptable range, performed reliably in urban traffic, and integrated smoothly into regular service routes. But the primary objective was not just operational feasibility, it was to evaluate whether hydrogen fuel could be sourced affordably, reliably, and sustainably for long-term fleet use. That’s where the project faltered.
Brussels lacked a dedicated hydrogen production facility, so fuel had to be delivered. While the city initially hoped to use green hydrogen, supply constraints made that impractical. Instead, it relied on trucked-in hydrogen, with uncertain emissions credentials and elevated costs. The delivered fuel was significantly more expensive per kilometer than diesel or electricity, and efforts to secure a consistent supply of green hydrogen proved unworkable. These supply-side limitations—scarcity, price volatility, and infrastructure complexity—undermined the case for hydrogen in the Brussels context.
By late 2023, STIB concluded that the challenges were too great. The pilot ended, the bus was withdrawn, and the agency confirmed it would not expand hydrogen use. Instead, STIB is focusing its decarbonization strategy on battery-electric buses, which benefit from existing grid infrastructure and a more stable cost profile.
500 kilometers away as the hydrogen airplane doesn’t fly,
Aberdeen
, Scotland, is hydrocarbon-heavy but hydrogen-light. Aberdeen was one of the first cities in Europe to deploy hydrogen-powered double-decker buses, beginning with 15 Wrightbus vehicles in 2020 and adding another 10 in 2022. The project was backed by EU funding under the JIVE program, despite Scotland being part of post-Brexit UK, and framed as a key step toward a zero-emission public transport system. The buses were intended to be fueled by locally produced green hydrogen, with the long-term goal of supporting a regional hydrogen economy centered around the Aberdeen Hydrogen Hub.
Despite early optimism, the project has encountered persistent challenges. Hydrogen fuel costs have been significantly higher than for diesel or battery-electric alternatives, with operational costs estimated to be around 40% higher per kilometer. These cost pressures were compounded by inconsistent fuel supply. Since July 2024, the entire hydrogen fleet has been inactive due to a shortage of hydrogen, leaving buses idle at the King Street depot. The local hydrogen hub, still under development in partnership with BP, has not come online quickly enough to support daily operations. As a result, the project, once viewed as a flagship for hydrogen mobility, is now constrained by the very infrastructure and fuel supply it hoped to catalyze.
The Rare “Successes”
Cologne
is one of the few relatively good news stories for hydrogen bus fleets. Regionalverkehr Köln (RVK) has become the largest operator of hydrogen fuel cell buses in Europe, with a fleet that reached 101 vehicles by late 2024 and is expected to grow to 160 by the end of 2025. This scale has been made possible by strong federal support, including nearly €34 million in subsidies aimed at promoting zero-emission transport. A key factor in RVK’s hydrogen strategy is the availability of industrial by-product hydrogen from chemical plants in nearby Hürth

data.title: 'Nobody has done this before': Britain's beloved steam trains trial technology
data.author: beardyw
data.article_summary: 文章主要报道了英国蒸汽火车尝试引入先进技术的试验。由于英国铁路信号系统正进行重大变革，传统的线路旁彩光信号将逐步被车载数字信号系统取代。为确保蒸汽火车能在未来继续运行，60163号“Tornado”蒸汽火车首次安装了欧洲列车控制系统（ETCS），该试验项目耗资约900万英镑。Tornado是世界上首台配备车载数字信号系统的蒸汽机车，试验过程中面临了诸如振动、高温、煤尘等环境挑战。项目团队克服了技术难题，成功将现代信号技术与传统蒸汽火车结合，展示了 heritage 和数字系统共存的可能性。该项目旨在确保蒸汽火车能适应未来的铁路运营环境。

The cab of the 60163 Tornado with (top left) an electronic screen.
Photograph: Hitachi Rail
View image in fullscreen
The cab of the 60163 Tornado with (top left) an electronic screen.
Photograph: Hitachi Rail
The Observer
Rail transport
‘Nobody has done this before’: Britain’s beloved steam trains trial pioneering technology
In-cab digital signalling was tested last week as part of a project to secure the future of main-line locomotives
Daniel Puddicombe
Sat 19 Apr 2025 10.00 EDT
Last modified on Sat 19 Apr 2025 11.23 EDT
Share
About 500 steam trains run across the UK each year, from Penzance in the south to Inverness in the north,
­transporting tens of thousands of passengers to a bygone age
, ­bringing joy to the faces of enthusiasts and bemusing commuters.
But the future of main line steam operations could be under threat unless the traditional fire-breathing machines can be fitted with pioneering modern technology.
The UK’s railways are undergoing a major change to their signalling ­systems in the coming years.
Network Rail
is planning to remove traditional lineside colour light signals in favour of in-cab signalling systems along key routes. No steam locomotive in the world had ever been run with in-cab digital signalling – until now.
On a Monday night earlier this month, the new technology was ­trialled for the first time as part of a “pathfinder” project aimed at ­securing the future of steam locomotives in the UK.
The “A1” No.60163 Tornado –
Britain’s first steam locomotive to be built in 50 years
and which has appeared in the
Paddington 2
movie and on
Top Gear
– has been ­fitted with European Train Control System (ETCS) technology as part of a Network Rail-led initiative which was launched in 2021. Fitting the new technology cost about £9m.
View image in fullscreen
The Tornado crosses the Ribblehead viaduct in the Yorkshire Dales.
Photograph: Danny Lawson/PA
ETCS is to be rolled out across the country in the coming years and some trains will run in digital-only mode from the end of this year.
It is already widely used in Europe and is seen as the industry standard ­signalling system for high-speed lines. Since 2011, the Cambrian Coast Line has been operated exclusively using the system as part of a different pilot programme.
The Tornado ran west of Shrewsbury to Newtown and Welshpool overnight to trial the technology for the first time.
“It is existential to the sector if steam cannot run with ETCS … the team have done a brilliant job of ­getting us to this point,” a Network Rail spokesperson involved in the project told the
Observer
. “The pathfinder [project] is all about saying ‘this is going to be really hard, is it ­technically viable?’ Nobody has ever done it with a heritage vehicle.”
Since the privatisation of the railways, steam trains have been free to roam the national network subject to there being “white space” in the ­timetables around service trains.
“We had quite a few challenges fitting the systems,” Rob Morland, electrical engineer at The A1 Steam Locomotive Trust, Tornado’s ­owning group, told the
Observer
. “This is a very harsh environment: we’ve got heat, coal, coal dust, shocks and vibrations and they all stress the systems.”
A second steam-powered turbo generator, an axle-driven alternator and a dedicated battery bank had to be installed in order to power the equipment: “The cab was stripped back to bare metal because of the sheer number of new conduits, boxes and equipment and that was the only practical way to do it,” Morland added.
Amy Clouston, principal human factors specialist at engineering consultancy AtkinsRéalis, which designed the fitment of the systems, said: “We had to test whether or not you can even use a touchscreen while you’re hurtling along at up to 75mph. We’ve had to think about vibrations, lighting, noise, coal dust, water and steam and grubby fingers.”
Clouston said her team also had to factor in the placement of the screens to avoid being hit by a fireman ­swinging a shovel around, while still being in a position where the driver can still see the safety-critical ­information displayed.
“Drivers have varied positions: some drivers hang out of the cab, ­others stand. It isn’t a ‘I’m sat at a desk’ design of a modern diesel or electric locomotive,” she said.
Keeping the computers powering the systems cool also proved to be a headache: “The design team had the challenge of sealing them [against] coal dust and heat. Electronics in a sealed environment that’s already hot does not bode well [for the longevity],” she added.
“Tornado’s retrofit with our ETCS is a world-first project that has tested our technology in one of the most complex and harsh ­operating environments, proving heritage and digital systems can coexist ­without compromise,” Tank Porteous, ­main line signalling programme director at Hitachi Rail UK, a partner in the project, said.

data.title: The most famous carbon dioxide absorber
data.author: bemmu
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讲述了1970年阿波罗13号任务的惊险故事。原本计划第三次登月的任务因爆炸导致三名宇航员被困在距地球20万英里的太空中。文章详细介绍了阿波罗13号飞船的构造，包括指挥舱、服务舱和登月舱，并解释了服务舱中的二氧化碳吸收器对宇航员生存的关键作用。由于飞船受损，宇航员利用有限材料自制了二氧化碳吸收器，最终成功返回地球。文章还简要提及了1969年阿波罗计划的首次登月以及飞船各部分的功能。

主要讨论点：Apollo 13故事及其技术细节，CO2吸收器，技术兼容性问题，以及对不同话题的延展讨论。

不同观点：
• **对CO2吸收器的需求**：[londons_explore]提出是否存在家用大小的CO2吸收器，以将室内CO2浓度降至工业化前水平（200ppm），而非城市房屋中常见的800ppm。这表明了对空气质量的关注。

• **对Apollo 13细节的兴趣**：[breakyerself]指出文章中关于降落伞减速的描述有误，实际应是热盾先通过大气层减速。这反映了对技术细节准确性的关注。[josefritzishere]则表示对Apollo 13故事细节的兴趣，特别是通过书籍或电影获取的信息。[jrflowers]以幽默方式评论了Neil Armstrong登月名言的错误引用。

• **技术兼容性问题**：[breput]提到过去阿波罗计划中过滤器的形状问题，并将其与现代太空舱中的宇航服不兼容问题进行对比，指出Boeing、SpaceX和NASA Orion之间的不兼容性。[teekert]认为这一技术不兼容的问题可以作为“医疗保健中的互操作性”演讲的引入例子。

• **历史技术背景**：[userbinator]提醒大家注意Apollo 13所使用的技术是1960年代的技术，暗示应以历史视角看待当时的技术水平。[hinkley]则简单提醒Apollo 13相关影片即将在Netflix下架，转移了讨论焦点。

补充讨论：
• **CO2吸收器的化学物质**：[wolfi1]提到传统的CO2吸收器使用的是氢氧化钾溶液，暗示这是更为人熟知的解决方案。

• **时间巧合的幽默**：[giraffe_lady]对Apollo 13发射时间（13:13）以及其潜在的迷信影响表示惊讶和调侃。

争议焦点：
• **技术细节的准确性**：讨论中涉及到Apollo 13降落过程中降落伞和热盾的作用顺序，这反映了对历史事件技术细节的不同理解和关注。

• **技术兼容性问题**：现代太空任务中设备和宇航服的不兼容性被视为一个值得注意的问题，反映了对技术标准化和互操作性的关注。

I have another website that may interest you. In addition to my interest in medical equipment, I am fascinated by psychology. I have made a website that explains the concept of “Happy Thinking”, which is about how one can find happiness by changing how one thinks. The website is free, and you can visit it by clicking the link below. I am confident it will help you find happiness!
Unless you are an anaesthetist, you probably wouldn’t know what a carbon dioxide absorber is (red arrow below).
However, for a brief period in the year 1970, carbon dioxide absorbers were what everyone was talking about. This is the story of Apollo 13 which blasted off in 1970 towards the Moon. However, things did not go according to plan and an explosion in the spacecraft left three astronauts stranded 200,000 miles from home. Suddenly this story became headline news. The whole world got to know how the astronaut’s survival depended on whether they could make a carbon dioxide absorber using the limited materials available in their spacecraft.
On July 21, 1969, Neil Armstrong stepped off the ladder of his spacecraft and became the first human to walk on the Moon. The first words spoken by him on the Moon that day are still remembered.
The first lunar landing was part of a series of space missions of the Apollo Space program. On April 11, 1970, it was the turn of Apollo 13 to lift off. This was going to be the third team to land on the Moon. The three astronauts (Lovell, Swigert, and Haise) for this mission were sitting on a massive rocket that would take them into outer space. The rocket (Saturn V), shown below, was about 110 meters tall (360 feet), had a diameter of about 10 meters (33 feet) and weighed about 3,000,000 kilograms (6,500,000 pounds). To appreciate the size of this mammoth rocket, compare its height with the man standing near it (tip of the red arrow).
If you are superstitious and believe that the number 13 is not lucky, then you will be forgiven for thinking that the launch time was rather “unlucky”. Apollo 13 launched at 13:13 ( North American Central Time Zone ).
The image shows the gigantic rocket launching into space.
Within one minute of lift-off, the rocket was travelling at the speed of sound. The rocket was built of various sections and as it went up into space, to avoid carrying unnecessary weight, it was designed to discard sections of itself that were no longer of any use (e.g. parts containing empty fuel tanks). Below is an image of a rocket throwing away a part of itself as it made its way to outer space. These massive pieces fell into the sea ( hopefully not hitting any fishermen below !).
Within about 15 minutes the astronauts reached outer space and started orbiting around Earth. Their orbiting spaceship would have looked like this.
The “spaceship” actually consisted of three parts. These parts will be briefly explained to you so that you will later better understand the drama that took place in this mission.
Let us begin with the “command module “. This is a rather cramped compartment (shown in green below) in which the three astronauts mostly travelled inside.
The command module was attached to a large section called the “service module “. This had an engine to take the astronauts towards the moon and back again towards Earth. Importantly, the service module also provided life-sustaining functions for the astronauts, such as giving oxygen, water and electricity.
The service module had tanks of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen. It also had special devices called “fuel cells”. These fuel cells were able to take hydrogen and oxygen from the tanks to produce water and electricity.
Here is a picture of an actual fuel cell.
So you can see that the service module provides vital supplies of oxygen, water, and electricity for the astronauts sitting in the command module.
Here is an actual picture of a command module and service module attached together.
The third part of the “spaceship” is the lunar module.
The lunar module is used to descend to the Moon, and of course, return back up as well. You will understand the role of the lunar module and the other parts better if I briefly describe to you how a typical Moon mission is expected to happen. Please note that Apollo 13 had a mishap and could not do what is described below. However, by understanding what should have happened, you will better understand the drama that happened.
So, if things went according to plan, the spaceship, with its three main components, would have arrived at the Moon and orbited around it.
Two of the astronauts would move into the lunar module. Unfortunately, one unlucky astronaut would have to remain back in the command module to look after it.

43687583.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讲述了1970年阿波罗13号任务的惊险故事。原本计划第三次登月的任务因爆炸导致三名宇航员被困在距地球20万英里的太空中。文章详细介绍了阿波罗13号飞船的构造，包括指挥舱、服务舱和登月舱，并解释了服务舱中的二氧化碳吸收器对宇航员生存的关键作用。由于飞船受损，宇航员利用有限材料自制了二氧化碳吸收器，最终成功返回地球。文章还简要提及了1969年阿波罗计划的首次登月以及飞船各部分的功能。
43687583.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apollo 13故事及其技术细节，CO2吸收器，技术兼容性问题，以及对不同话题的延展讨论。

不同观点：
• **对CO2吸收器的需求**：[londons_explore]提出是否存在家用大小的CO2吸收器，以将室内CO2浓度降至工业化前水平（200ppm），而非城市房屋中常见的800ppm。这表明了对空气质量的关注。

• **对Apollo 13细节的兴趣**：[breakyerself]指出文章中关于降落伞减速的描述有误，实际应是热盾先通过大气层减速。这反映了对技术细节准确性的关注。[josefritzishere]则表示对Apollo 13故事细节的兴趣，特别是通过书籍或电影获取的信息。[jrflowers]以幽默方式评论了Neil Armstrong登月名言的错误引用。

• **技术兼容性问题**：[breput]提到过去阿波罗计划中过滤器的形状问题，并将其与现代太空舱中的宇航服不兼容问题进行对比，指出Boeing、SpaceX和NASA Orion之间的不兼容性。[teekert]认为这一技术不兼容的问题可以作为“医疗保健中的互操作性”演讲的引入例子。

• **历史技术背景**：[userbinator]提醒大家注意Apollo 13所使用的技术是1960年代的技术，暗示应以历史视角看待当时的技术水平。[hinkley]则简单提醒Apollo 13相关影片即将在Netflix下架，转移了讨论焦点。

补充讨论：
• **CO2吸收器的化学物质**：[wolfi1]提到传统的CO2吸收器使用的是氢氧化钾溶液，暗示这是更为人熟知的解决方案。

• **时间巧合的幽默**：[giraffe_lady]对Apollo 13发射时间（13:13）以及其潜在的迷信影响表示惊讶和调侃。

争议焦点：
• **技术细节的准确性**：讨论中涉及到Apollo 13降落过程中降落伞和热盾的作用顺序，这反映了对历史事件技术细节的不同理解和关注。

• **技术兼容性问题**：现代太空任务中设备和宇航服的不兼容性被视为一个值得注意的问题，反映了对技术标准化和互操作性的关注。

data.article_summary: 文章报道了奥运金牌得主、短跑名将Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce在一场她孩子学校运动日上的100米比赛中完胜其他家长的趣事。她没有像一些运动员那样在终点前炫耀或放松，而是全力以赴。这凸显了职业运动员与业余爱好者之间的巨大差距。文章还引用了网友评论，有人回忆起观看顶级运动员比赛的震撼体验，强调了亲眼观看高水平比赛的难得。

不同观点：

Olympic Gold Medalist Dominates the 100m at Her Kid’s Sports Day Event
If you’re one of those people who watches the Olympics and wishes they’d put a normal person in the competition so we can see how fast the athletes really are, this one’s for you.
Eight-time Olympic gold medalist and a 10-time world champion sprinter Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce
recently announced her comeback
and for her first 100m race, she
competed against the other parents
at her son’s sports day event.
And completely demolished them
.
I love how she goes flat-out…no Usain Bolt showboating or looking around near the finish line. All business. (via
@rebeccablood.bsky.social
)
Update:
She did it back in 2023 too.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Windows 11升级中的安全要求和兼容性问题

不同观点：
• [支持升级和安全要求] 
  - [4rt] 认为强制升级到Windows 11并遵循现代安全卫生标准是必要的，即使需要强力推行。
  
• [转向Linux]
  - [conartist6] 表示在使用Windows作为主要桌面操作系统25年后，决定转向Linux，主要是为了运行Steam。这表明部分用户因Windows 11的升级要求而选择其他操作系统。

data.title: UML diagram for the DDD example in Evans' book
data.author: takaakit
data.article_summary:
这篇文章介绍了使用UML图表来展示Eric Evans书籍《领域驱动设计》中货运系统示例的结构和行为。该项目基于GitHub上的dddsample-core项目代码，帮助理解领域驱动设计（DDD）的战略和战术设计实现及运作机制。文章提到了几个关键的UML图表：

1. **用户-系统交互图**：展示用户与系统之间的主要交互，包括货物追踪和预订新货物。
2. **领域模型概览图**：展示领域模型的基本元素及其关系，隐藏了属性和操作以聚焦于元素间的关系。
3. **货物"ABC123"的领域对象图**：展示具体货物对象及其连接，示例中货物正从香港运往赫尔辛基，目前在纽约港。
4. **整体结构图**：展示货运系统的总体结构，包括预订和运输网络两个上下文，使用Spring项目实现。
5. **行为图**：包括系统初始化、货物追踪、货物预订、路线建议和路线分配等场景的通信图。

文章还提到使用Astah Professional/UML工具查看详细模型文件和创建类似图表的方法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：UML及其在系统建模和架构设计中的应用与价值

不同观点：
• **neilv** 认为UML在系统建模中仍然具有重要价值，尤其是在高价值系统或复杂系统的沟通和错误排查中非常有效。他指出，UML图中的错误可能导致严重后果，且UML不应被视为仅用于销售或高层展示的工具。如果仅依赖模糊的术语进行沟通，可能导致项目失败或技术债务。

• **alganet** 提出简化UML使用的观点，认为好的UML应该是简单的，部分图表可以省略或简化，尤其是当团队已经熟悉相关内容时。他还认为，有时代码本身已经足够清晰，不需要额外的图表，且完美的UML图往往是“一次性”的，不必长期维护。

• **ak_111** 提到UML在企业计算中曾经非常流行，但如今似乎已经消失，并询问其替代方案。这引发了对UML是否仍然适用以及当前使用什么工具或方法进行系统建模的讨论。

• **BerislavLopac** 推荐使用C4模型而非UML，认为C4模型在符号和组件建模方面更具灵活性。他还提到IcePanel作为工具的优点，表明有其他现代工具可以替代UML用于架构文档。

• **stevoski** 通过一个对话示例指出，即使领域专家在初始沟通中确认了UML图的正确性，实际使用系统时仍可能发现新的问题，显示出UML在实际应用中可能存在的局限性。

• **firesteelrain** 支持UML的使用，认为如果理解符号和关系，UML图非常容易沟通，且可以有效与非技术人员交流。

• 技术进步：提到AI模型在UML图生成中的应用，显示出技术进步对传统建模工具的影响。

• UML的实际应用价值及其是否已被更现代的工具或方法取代。

UML Diagram for the DDD Example in Evans' Book
This project uses UML diagrams to illustrate the structure and behavior of the DDD example—a cargo shipping system—from Eric Evans' book (
Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
). These diagrams are created based on the source code of the
dddsample-core
project on GitHub. They aim to help us understand how the example implements the strategic and tactical designs of DDD and the mechanisms by which it operates.
If you want to get into DDD theory, check out Evans' book. If you want to get into the implementation details, check out the source code of the dddsample-core project. Also, if you want to understand the UML model behind these diagrams, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool
Astah Professional/UML/Viewer
.
Clicking on the UML diagram image below opens the corresponding diagram in Diagram Map
*1
.
*1
: Diagram Map allows you to zoom and pan, like Google Maps, when viewing a UML diagram. You can view it with any browser. To create one on your own,
Astah Professional/UML
and the
m+ plug-in
are required.
User-system interaction
This sequence diagram illustrates the key interactions between the user and the system, with references to other diagrams. The interactions show two use cases: (1) tracking the handling of specified cargo, and (2) booking new cargo followed by assigning it a delivery route. To understand the system specifications in more detail, refer to Chapter 7 of Evans' book, Using the Language in an Example: A Cargo Shipping System.
Domain model overview
This class diagram illustrates the basic elements of the domain model and their relationships. The layout of the domain model elements is based on the diagram presented in the dddsample-core project. Attributes and operations are hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Domain objects for "ABC123" cargo
This object diagram shows the basic domain objects and thier connections. In particular, it shows the object snapshot associated with the cargo object "ABC123," which is preset as sample data. The cargo "ABC123," which is en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Overall structure
This class diagram illustrates the overall structure of the cargo shipping system: it is composed of two contexts, the Booking context and the Transport network context. The system is implemented using Spring projects such as Spring Boot / MVC / Data JPA. Note that this diagram focuses on elements and relationships that may be considered and does not reflect the entire implementation. Attributes and operations are also hidden to focus on understanding the elements and their relationships. If you want to see them, open the model file (ddd-example-in-evans-book.asta) using the modeling tool Astah.
Behavior 1: Initialization
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user launches the cargo shipping system, with a focus on messages that may be worth considering.
Behavior 2: Cargo tracking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user requests tracking for cargo "ABC123" on the cargo tracking page. The cargo "ABC123," which is preset by the system and en route from HongKong to Helsinki, is currently at the port of New York, where unloading has been completed.
Behavior 3-1: Cargo booking
This communication diagram shows a scenario in which the user registers new cargo on the cargo booking page. The new cargo is set to be shipped from New York to Helsinki.
Behavior 3-2: Route suggestion
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user requests cargo routing on the cargo booking result page, followed by the suggestion of route candidates.
Behavior 3-3: Route assignment
This communication diagram illustrates a scenario in which the user requests the assignment of new cargo to a delivery route on the route selection page.

这篇文章介绍了使用UML图表来展示Eric Evans书籍《领域驱动设计》中货运系统示例的结构和行为。该项目基于GitHub上的dddsample-core项目代码，帮助理解领域驱动设计（DDD）的战略和战术设计实现及运作机制。文章提到了几个关键的UML图表：

1. **用户-系统交互图**：展示用户与系统之间的主要交互，包括货物追踪和预订新货物。
2. **领域模型概览图**：展示领域模型的基本元素及其关系，隐藏了属性和操作以聚焦于元素间的关系。
3. **货物"ABC123"的领域对象图**：展示具体货物对象及其连接，示例中货物正从香港运往赫尔辛基，目前在纽约港。
4. **整体结构图**：展示货运系统的总体结构，包括预订和运输网络两个上下文，使用Spring项目实现。
5. **行为图**：包括系统初始化、货物追踪、货物预订、路线建议和路线分配等场景的通信图。

文章还提到使用Astah Professional/UML工具查看详细模型文件和创建类似图表的方法。

data.title: Why is OpenAI buying Windsurf?
data.author: theahura
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 可能以30亿美元收购 Windsurf 及其相关技术和竞争格局

不同观点：
• [_jab] 的观点：
  1. 认为这些公司的护城河（moat）很浅，自动完成功能的核心在于如何在延迟和模型质量之间权衡。
  2. GPT 4.1 可能是自动完成功能的有力竞争者，Windsurf 也计划使用 GPT 4.1。
  3. 收购可能以股票形式进行，而非现金交易。
  4. 如果代理流（agentic flows）功能取得成功，数据将成为更重要的护城河，因为这些工具可以收集用户编码方式的遥测数据。

• [kace91] 的观点：
  1. 对不同工具之间的差异只有1-2%的观点持怀疑态度，认为 Cursor 和 Copilot 之间的差异远大于1%。
  2. 其公司员工宁愿自费购买 Cursor 也不使用免费的 Copilot，证明了这一点。

• [mrcwinn] 的观点：
  1. 认为30亿美元的收购价并非不合理，关键在于未来该产品的潜在价值。
  2. Cursor 与 Anthropic 的密切关系可能使 OpenAI 希望通过收购来消除竞争。

• [WA] 的观点：
  1. 认为30亿美元的收购证明这些工具目前还不能替代程序员。
  2. 如果工具能如预期那样工作，OpenAI 无需花费如此巨资。

• [g8oz] 的观点：
  1. 将此次收购比作 Snowflake 收购 Streamlit，认为这是购买者内部执行放缓的迹象。

• [phillipcarter] 的观点：
  1. 认为 OpenAI 希望通过收购 Windsurf 来扩大其在开发者中的影响力，避免被视为仅是“ChatGPT 公司”。
  2. 当前的投入比未来更划算。

• [ramoz] 的观点：
  1. 认为收购 Windsurf 可以进入企业市场，覆盖广泛用户群，并获取训练数据。
  2. 这些 IDE 有可能成为下一代通用办公工具。

• [consumer451] 的观点：
  1. 提供 Windsurf CEO 的采访链接，未提及是否涉及收购。

• [firesteelrain] 的观点：
  1. Windsurf/Codeium 的企业版可以在公司自有硬件上运行，有助于隐私和专有数据保护。
  2. 这种模式有可能带来大量付费客户，但能否达到400亿美元市值 unclear。

• [croes] 的观点：
  1. 认为如果 AI 能做到，那么30亿美元应该足够从零开始开发。

• [apples_oranges] 的观点：
  1. 认为收购的主要原因通常是人才，而非软件本身。

• [jchonphoenix] 的观点：
  1. 猜测收购是为了获取遥测数据，以减少未来在 Mercor 上的巨额开支。

• [xnx] 的观点：
  1. 认为30亿美元的数字更多是营销手段，以展示 OpenAI 的重要性和实力。
  2. 希望 Windsurf 能从中获得实际收益。

• [dstroot] 的观点：
  1. 当前使用 Claude 代码和 Cursor，但 VSCode 正在迅速追赶。
  2. 理想情况下，希望 VSCode 具备强大的代理功能，并支持自带 LLM 的功能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于30亿美元的收购价是否合理，以及这些工具是否能如预期那样替代程序员的工作。
• 讨论还涉及收购的形式（现金 vs 股票）以及收购的战略意义（获取数据、消除竞争、进入企业市场）。
• 不同用户对工具之间的差异和实用性有不同看法，反映了市场竞争的复杂性。

data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了欧洲土壤健康问题，尤其是西班牙的土壤退化状况。欧盟60-70%的土壤处于不健康状态，导致每年约€500亿的损失。西班牙是土壤侵蚀最严重的国家，每年每公顷流失约14.2吨土壤。地理学家Jesús Rodrigo Comino通过地理绘图系统和人工智能研究葡萄园的土壤侵蚀，致力于开发可持续的土壤管理实践，帮助农民做出决策，如灌溉和种植覆盖作物。他还参与了欧盟的SOILCRATES项目，旨在通过实验提高人们对土壤健康的认识。气候变化对土壤健康的影响日益显著，如气温升高和极端降雨事件增加。尽管有些农民开始采用良好实践，但仍需更多努力改善土壤质量。

主要讨论点：土壤健康与管理、技术在农业中的应用、以及不同种植方法的比较

不同观点：
• [econ] 提出历史上可能存在以土壤为核心的先进文明，例如Terra Preta，并认为人类在足够时间下可以解决很多问题。
• [tbrownaw] 关注使用地理 mapping 系统和人工智能（AI）来评估葡萄园的土壤侵蚀和退化问题，并提到像 GitHub Copilot 这样的工具在代码设计中的应用。
• [bgnn] 分享了个人从盆栽到土壤种植的经验，强调了使用无挖耕作、绿肥和覆盖作物等方式成功改善土壤质量，但也指出过程中的挑战和不稳定性。
• [photochemsyn] 提出在工业和矿业历史悠久的地区，重金属污染对土壤健康的影响是一个被忽视的重大健康风险，并引用了相关文献支持这一观点。
• [pfdietz] 讲述了个人经历，说明良好的土壤可以提高房产价值，并提到添加叶霉可以改善土壤的保水性。
• [ralusek] 认为土壤健康等因素对植物健康并非直接必要，而是使环境自给自足。他比较了合成肥料和培养良好土壤的不同种植方法，强调了自我维持土壤的优点。
• [bethekidyouwant] 批评有关健康土壤的文章缺乏实质内容，并指出大规模有机种植需要大量人工劳动，与小规模种植不同。
• [SwayamDas] 列出了有机物、微生物、土壤动物、营养元素、土壤结构和水管理是健康土壤的关键组成部分。
• [zeristor] 提到文章中对AI和其他数据来源的使用案例不足，并期待未来在数据访问和处理方面的技术发展。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是土壤健康与植物生长的直接关系，[ralusek] 认为合成肥料和良好排水性土壤足以支持植物生长，而 [bgnn] 和 [SwayamDas] 则强调了培养自给自足土壤的长远好处。
• [photochemsyn] 提出的重金属污染风险在讨论中是一个重要的环境和健康问题，但其他评论者未对此做出回应。
• 技术在农业中的应用，如AI和地理 mapping 系统，是一个潜在的发展方向，[tbrownaw] 和 [zeristor] 对此表示关注，并希望看到更多实际应用案例。

这些观点展示了在土壤管理和农业技术应用方面的多样化视角和实际经验，同时也揭示了当前在这一领域存在的争议和未解问题。

Soil quality is crucial for sustaining production in vineyards, such as this one near Montilla in southern Spain.
Credit: JORGE GUERRERO/AFP via Getty
When it comes to the land, the European Union faces a reckoning: 60–70% of its soils are considered unhealthy, resulting in soil degradation. That costs €50 billion (US$55 billion) annually because of the loss of essential services and the effect on human health. Spain has the highest rates of soil degradation in Europe, with an average of 14.2 tonnes of soil lost per hectare to erosion each year
1
. Although its importance is often overlooked, quality soil is essential for sustaining agriculture and crucial ecosystems. Its importance was highlighted in the 2015 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, with soil health named as a key factor in achieving several of the goals.
Nature Spotlight: Spain
Having studied soil erosion in vineyards across Europe, Jesús Rodrigo Comino, a geographer at the University of Granada, Spain, is hoping to unearth a solution. Now he works with farmers, researchers and policymakers to test and use more-sustainable soil-management practices in vineyards and more broadly. Rodrigo Comino speaks to
Nature
about his research programme and why healthy soils are important for Spain’s cultural heritage and economy.
Tell us about your work in soil science.
I was always a curious kid, but my passion for soil science began with my studies at the University of Malaga in Spain and at Trier University in Germany. My home region of Andalusia in Spain has some really beautiful landscapes, but some areas are heavily degraded because of soil erosion and other factors. I felt compelled to find solutions to these problems.
When I came back to Spain in 2021 after doing my PhD and a postdoctoral position in Germany, I started a project to assess soil erosion and degradation in vineyards using geographical mapping systems and artificial intelligence (AI). Soil erosion is caused by natural factors, such as extreme rainfall events and strong winds, as well as by human-driven activities, including tillage and urbanization. AI helps me to design and polish the software codes that I use to create geographical maps and analyse data. The main idea is to develop tools to help farmers make decisions. These might be about how to apply irrigation systems; which types of cover crop to plant; or when to till the soil, if necessary, to prevent soil degradation.
Geographer Jesús Rodrigo Comino examines the soil at a vineyard.
Credit: Jesús Rodrigo Comino
I’m also involved in a Soil Living Labs project called SOILCRATES, which is part of an EU mission called A Soil Deal for Europe. The goal is to create field sites where soil scientists, agronomists, stakeholders and policymakers come together to conduct experiments and establish plots with sustainable soils. As part of the project, we also aim to show people how important fertile soils are to their lives and how their actions can affect soil health. The EU is now investing in a variety of projects to improve soil quality and enhance people’s understanding of soil. I’ve seen people implementing good practices to reduce soil erosion. But we’re not there yet — much more work is needed.
How has climate change affected your work?
It is evident that many places, especially urban ones, are experiencing an increase in temperature and a reduction in precipitation volume. We’re also seeing a concentration of extreme rainfall events in short periods of time, such as the flooding that happened in Valencia in Spain last year. All of these factors can affect soil health.
When it comes to the vineyards in Spain, we don’t yet have enough data to confirm whether and how climate change is altering them — but the trends are clear. We know that vineyards are encountering higher temperatures now than they did in the past, and that this is causing the vines to flower earlier. Annual rainfall is being concentrated into shorter time periods, and we’re also experiencing extreme rainfall events, which cause soil erosion.
What are farmers telling you about their experiences?

data.title: Gemma 3 QAT Models: Bringing AI to Consumer GPUs
data.author: emrah
data.article_summary: Gemma 3 QAT模型通过量化感知训练（QAT）技术，显著降低了内存需求，使大型AI模型（如Gemma 3 27B）能够在消费级GPU（如NVIDIA RTX 3090）上运行。传统BFloat16（BF16）精度需要大量VRAM，而通过QAT，模型参数可被压缩至4位（int4），从而大幅减少GPU内存占用。例如，Gemma 3 27B模型从54 GB（BF16）降至14.1 GB（int4）。这种优化使得高性能AI模型在个人设备上运行成为可能，提升了模型的可访问性和实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gemma-3-27b-it-qat-4bit模型的性能、资源利用及其与其他模型（如Mistral、Llama 4）的对比。

不同观点：
• Simonw认为Gemma-3-27b-it-qat-4bit是他目前最喜欢的本地模型之一，与Mistral Small 3.1 24B不相上下。他提到该模型在M2 64GB设备上表现优异，且内存占用较少，可以同时运行其他应用程序。他还分享了使用该模型自动生成LLM工具插件的实例。
• Diggan指出，尽管文章讨论了不同模型在BF16精度和QAT模型上的VRAM使用情况，但缺少BF16和QAT模型之间质量对比的数据，而这正是读者关心的核心问题。
• Porphyra调侃微软和苹果之前推广AI硬件，但实际上消费级GPU才刚开始支持高性能模型，如Gemma-3-27b-it-qat-4bit。
• Trebligdivad在AMD 3950x CPU上运行Gemma-3，发现其在翻译和图像描述方面表现出色，但有时输出过于冗长，需要明确指示才能获得简洁的结果。
• Mythz提到在Ollama上运行QAT Gemma3:27b后，性能提升了1.47倍，从13.72 tok/s提升到20.11 tok/s。
• Behnamoh认为公司应对本地LLM给予更多支持，但指出文章中关于DeepSeek r1在FP16下所需H100数量的图表具有误导性，因为该模型实际使用的是FP8。
• Mekpro认为Gemma 3比Llama 4优秀，因为后者模型体积过大，限制了其在GPU VRAM有限的用户中的应用，而Gemma 3则更为广泛适用。
• Emrah仅提供了Gemma3在Ollama上的链接。
• Miki123211询问在多用户API场景中如何最大化GPU利用率部署该模型，并提到其组织对数据驻留有严格要求。
• 999900000999认为如果Gemma模型能与Claude最新版本媲美，并持续运行代码，每月可节省600至700美元，建议公司使用本地LMS。
• Umajho使用Q4_K_M量化版本的Gemma-3-27b-it，发现其表现优于之前的DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B，并希望看到更多与未优化Q4版本的对比数据。
• Holografix询问16GB VRAM是否足够运行27b QAT版本。
• Justanotheratom好奇是否有人将此类模型打包到iPhone应用中，并关心 tokens/sec 的表现。
• Noodletheworld质疑这些模型早已发布，认为文章可能只是一篇跟进的博客，询问是否有其他新意。
• Alifatisk询问Gemma模型除了轻量级之外，是否有其他特别擅长的功能或优势。

补充讨论：
• 关于Gemma-3-27b-it-qat-4bit模型的质量、性能、资源利用及与其他模型的对比是讨论的核心。
• 争议焦点包括模型质量对比数据的缺失以及模型发布时间的质疑。
• 实用性方面，讨论了在不同硬件配置和应用场景中的部署问题，如多用户API场景和移动设备上的应用。

Gemma 3 QAT Models: Bringing state-of-the-Art AI to consumer GPUs
APR 18, 2025
Edouard YVINEC
Research Scientist
Phil Culliton
ML Engineer
Share
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Mail
Last month, we launched Gemma 3, our latest generation of open models. Delivering state-of-the-art performance, Gemma 3 quickly established itself as a leading model capable of running on a single high-end GPU like the NVIDIA H100 using its native BFloat16 (BF16) precision.
To make Gemma 3 even more accessible, we are announcing new versions optimized with Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) that dramatically reduces memory requirements while maintaining high quality. This enables you to run powerful models like Gemma 3 27B locally on consumer-grade GPUs like the NVIDIA RTX 3090.
This chart ranks AI models by Chatbot Arena Elo scores; higher scores (top numbers) indicate greater user preference. Dots show estimated NVIDIA H100 GPU requirements.
Understanding performance, precision, and quantization
The chart above shows the performance (Elo score) of recently released large language models. Higher bars mean better performance in comparisons as rated by humans viewing side-by-side responses from two anonymous models. Below each bar, we indicate the estimated number of NVIDIA H100 GPUs needed to run that model using the BF16 data type.
Why BFloat16 for this comparison?
BF16 is a common numerical format used during inference of many large models. It means that the model parameters are represented with 16 bits of precision. Using BF16 for all models helps us to make an apples-to-apples comparison of models in a common inference setup. This allows us to compare the inherent capabilities of the models themselves, removing variables like different hardware or optimization techniques like quantization, which we'll discuss next.
It's important to note that while this chart uses BF16 for a fair comparison, deploying the very largest models often involves using lower-precision formats like FP8 as a practical necessity to reduce immense hardware requirements (like the number of GPUs), potentially accepting a performance trade-off for feasibility.
The Need for Accessibility
While top performance on high-end hardware is great for cloud deployments and research, we heard you loud and clear: you want the power of Gemma 3 on the hardware you already own. We're committed to making powerful AI accessible, and that means enabling efficient performance on the consumer-grade GPUs found in desktops, laptops, and even phones.
Performance Meets Accessibility with Quantization-Aware Training in Gemma 3
This is where quantization comes in. In AI models, quantization reduces the precision of the numbers (the model's parameters) it stores and uses to calculate responses. Think of quantization like compressing an image by reducing the number of colors it uses. Instead of using 16 bits per number (BFloat16), we can use fewer bits, like 8 (int8) or even 4 (int4).
Using int4 means each number is represented using only 4 bits – a 4x reduction in data size compared to BF16. Quantization can often lead to performance degradation, so we’re excited to release Gemma 3 models that are robust to quantization. We released several quantized variants for each Gemma 3 model to enable inference with your favorite inference engine, such as Q4_0 (a common quantization format) for Ollama, llama.cpp, and MLX.
How do we maintain quality?
We use QAT. Instead of just quantizing the model after it's fully trained, QAT incorporates the quantization process during training. QAT simulates low-precision operations during training to allow quantization with less degradation afterwards for smaller, faster models while maintaining accuracy. Diving deeper, we applied QAT on ~5,000 steps using probabilities from the non-quantized checkpoint as targets. We reduce the perplexity drop by 54% (using llama.cpp perplexity evaluation) when quantizing down to Q4_0.
See the Difference: Massive VRAM Savings
The impact of int4 quantization is dramatic. Look at the VRAM (GPU memory) required just to load the model weights:

Drops from 54 GB (BF16) to just
14.1 GB
(int4)
Gemma 3 12B:
Shrinks from 24 GB (BF16) to only
6.6 GB
(int4)

Reduces from 8 GB (BF16) to a lean
2.6 GB
(int4)

Goes from 2 GB (BF16) down to a tiny

(int4)
Note:
This figure only represents the VRAM required to load the model weights. Running the model also requires additional VRAM for the KV cache, which stores information about the ongoing conversation and depends on the context length

These dramatic reductions unlock the ability to run larger, powerful models on widely available consumer hardware:

data.title: Three Felonies a Day (2013)
data.author: zekrioca
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了波士顿民权律师Harvey Silverglate的书《Three Felonies A Day》，书中指出，普通美国人在日常生活中不知不觉地犯下多项联邦重罪，因为现代联邦刑法数量庞大且定义模糊。Silverglate解释，联邦法律的复杂性和广泛性使得检察官可以对任何人提起指控，即使其行为看似无害。文章还提到QWest公司CEO Joseph P. Nacchio因拒绝配合NSA的大规模监控要求而被政府以证券交易内幕罪起诉并入狱的案例，强调了这种法律环境对公民自由的威胁。文章最后提到《华尔街日报》也在关注联邦刑法扩展及其后果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：普通人是否每天无意中犯下三项重罪，以及法律是否过于宽泛

不同观点：
• hn_throwaway_99：认为博客帖子在没有提供具体证据或例子（如普通人每天犯三项重罪的具体行为）的情况下，做出了大胆的断言。对约瑟夫·纳奇奥的案例分析过于片面，未考虑其可能确实犯了严重罪行。同时，单一案例（CEO因内幕交易被起诉）不能支持普遍性结论。
• ericyd：认为即便是简短的书评，也应给出一些日常生活中人们可能犯下的重罪例子，否则感觉像是在故意吊人胃口。
• hermannj314：分享了自己在美国的经历，试图用现金支付MRI费用以加快预约过程，却被视为保险欺诈，而在卢森堡这种做法是正常的，反映了美国法律的复杂和不透明。
• prmph：提供了多个日常行为可能构成犯罪的例子，如超速、未支付赠与税、上班时间浏览非工作相关网站、乱穿马路等，支持了普通人可能无意中犯下多项罪行的观点。
• qingcharles：指出在伊利诺伊州及其他州，违反网站的使用条款可能构成计算机篡改罪，进一步支持了法律可能过于宽泛的观点。
• djha-skin：将帖子视为对2013年爱德华·斯诺登事件的反应，认为其是对NSA获取数据手段的指责，并分享了其父亲对斯诺登的负面看法。
• fastaguy88：认为很多违法行为并非重罪，如超速、上班时间浏览非工作相关网站、因宿醉请病假等，并表示自己不太可能无意中犯下多项重罪。
• kazinator：引用俄罗斯谚语“只要有人的地方，就有可以定罪的法律条文”，支持了法律可能过于宽泛的观点。
• metadat：提到之前已有讨论，并给出链接。
• wcfrobert：提供了其他例子，如不报告大额现金交易、使用他人ID、下载盗版内容等，支持了普通人可能无意中犯下多项罪行的观点。

• 对约瑟夫·纳奇奥案例的不同解读反映了人们对法律和司法系统的不同看法。

You Commit Three Felonies a Day
In a book called
Three Felonies A Day
, Boston civil rights lawyer Harvey Silverglate says that everyone in the US commits felonies everyday and if the government takes a dislike to you for any reason, they’ll dig in and find a felony you’re guilty of.
The average professional in this country wakes up in the morning, goes to work, comes home, eats dinner, and then goes to sleep, unaware that he or she has likely committed several federal crimes that day. Why? The answer lies in the very nature of modern federal criminal laws, which have exploded in number but also become impossibly broad and vague. In Three Felonies a Day, Harvey A. Silverglate reveals how federal criminal laws have become dangerously disconnected from the English common law tradition and how prosecutors can pin arguable federal crimes on any one of us, for even the most seemingly innocuous behavior. The volume of federal crimes in recent decades has increased well beyond the statute books and into the morass of the Code of Federal Regulations, handing federal prosecutors an additional trove of vague and exceedingly complex and technical prohibitions to stick on their hapless targets. The dangers spelled out in Three Felonies a Day do not apply solely to “white collar criminals,” state and local politicians, and professionals. No social class or profession is safe from this troubling form of social control by the executive branch, and nothing less than the integrity of our constitutional democracy hangs in the balance.
In response to a question about what happens to big company CEOs who refuse to go along with government surveillance requests, John Gilmore
offers a case study
in what Silverglate is talking about.
We know what happened in the case of QWest before 9/11. They contacted the CEO/Chairman asking to wiretap all the customers. After he consulted with Legal, he refused. As a result, NSA canceled a bunch of unrelated billion dollar contracts that QWest was the top bidder for. And then the DoJ targeted him and prosecuted him and put him in prison for insider trading — on the theory that he knew of anticipated income from secret programs that QWest was planning for the government, while the public didn’t because it was classified and he couldn’t legally tell them, and then he bought or sold QWest stock knowing those things.
This CEO’s name is Joseph P. Nacchio and TODAY he’s still serving a trumped-up 6-year federal prison sentence today for quietly refusing an NSA demand to massively wiretap his customers.
You combine this with the uber-surveillance allegedly being undertaken by the NSA and other governmental agencies and you’ve got a system for more or less automatically accusing any US citizen of a felony. Free society, LOL ROFLcopter.
Update:
For the past two years, the Wall Street Journal has been
“examining the vastly expanding federal criminal law book and its consequences”
. (thx, jesse)

data.title: A 1980s toy robot arm inspired modern robotics
data.author: danso
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者童年时在Radio Shack发现的一款经典玩具——Armatron机械臂，这款1984年推出的玩具通过双操纵杆控制，可以实现旋转、弯曲、抓取等动作，尽管看似复杂，内部却几乎全靠机械结构实现。作者后来联系到Armatron的设计者，日本工程师渡边弘之，他已在Tomy公司工作49年，参与了多款经典电子玩具的开发。渡边透露，Armatron的灵感来自一篇关于机械臂的报纸剪报，最初设计与最终产品有很大不同，他借鉴了遥控直升机的操控原理，最终实现了机械臂的灵活运动。尽管渡边被视为主要发明者，但他强调这是团队合作的成果。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Armatron玩具的回忆、其对科技兴趣的启发、现代机器人技术的教育工具推荐以及对该玩具机制的现代技术复现讨论。

不同观点：
• [怀旧与启发] 一些用户（如brk、EncomLab、pryelluw）回忆了玩Armatron玩具的经历，认为该玩具通过其机械结构激发了他们对机器人技术或机械设计的兴趣。brk特别提到该玩具没有电子元件，完全依赖机械结构，这让他感到意外。
• [教育价值比较] fmajid认为Armatron的教育内容不如Apple II+，暗示现代技术设备可能提供更丰富的学习体验。
• [现代教育工具推荐] A4ET8a8uTh0_v2和victor106关注现代儿童如何入门机器人技术，询问适合5岁以上儿童的机器人工具包推荐，反映出当今选择过多与过去资源稀缺的对比。
• [技术复现与改进] WillAdams和gene-h讨论了使用现代技术（如Lego Technic和电子离合器）复现或改进Armatron机制的可能性，显示出对传统机械玩具的现代技术升级兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [噪音问题] eterpstra提到Armatron操作时的噪音问题，尽管控制良好，但噪音体验不佳。
• [链接分享] 一些用户（如brudgers、thedougd、irickt）分享了与Armatron相关的网页链接，提供了更多背景信息和变种版本。
• [网站问题] petermcneeley提到网页上出现巨大的订阅横幅，可能是一个技术问题，与其他讨论关系不大。

争议焦点：
• 该玩具的教育价值和现代技术设备的对比是潜在的争议点，特别是在fmajid提到Apple II+时，涉及到不同时代技术对教育的影响。

As a child of an electronic engineer, I spent a
lot
of time in our local Radio Shack as a kid. While my dad was locating capacitors and resistors, I was in the toy section. It was there, in 1984, that I discovered the best toy of my childhood: the Armatron robotic arm.
A drawing from the patent application for the Armatron robotic arm.
COURTESY OF TAKARA TOMY
Described as a “robot-like arm to aid young masterminds in scientific and laboratory experiments,” it was the rare toy that lived up to the hype printed on the front of the box. This was a legit
robotic arm.
You could rotate the arm to spin around its base, tilt it up and down, bend it at the “elbow” joint, rotate the “wrist,” and open and close the bright-­orange articulated hand in elegant chords of movement, all using only the twistable twin joysticks.
Anyone who played with this toy will also remember the sound it made. Once you slid the power button to the On position, you heard a constant whirring sound of plastic gears turning and twisting. And if you tried to push it past its boundaries, it twitched and protested with a jarring “CLICK … CLICK … CLICK.”
It wasn’t just kids who found the Armatron so special. It was featured on the cover of the
November/December 1982 issue
of
Robotics Age
magazine, which noted that the $31.95 toy (about $96 today) had “capabilities usually found only in much more expensive experimental arms.”
JIM GOLDEN
A few years ago I found my Armatron, and when I opened the case to get it working again, I was startled to find that other than the compartment for the pair of D-cell batteries, a switch, and a tiny three-volt DC motor, this thing was totally devoid of any electronic components. It was purely mechanical. Later, I found the patent
drawings
for the Armatron online and saw how incredibly complex the schematics of the gearbox were. This design was the work of a genius—or a madman.
The man behind the arm
I needed to know the story of this toy. I reached out to the manufacturer, Tomy (now known as Takara Tomy), which has been in business in Japan for over 100 years. It put me in touch with Hiroyuki Watanabe, a 69-year-old engineer and toy designer living in Tokyo. He’s retired now, but he worked at Tomy for 49 years, building many classic handheld electronic toys of the ’80s, including Blip,
Digital Diamond
,
Digital Derby
, and
Missile Strike
. Watanabe’s name can be found on
44 patents
, and he was involved in bringing between 50 and 60 products to market. Watanabe answered emailed questions via video, and his responses were translated from Japanese.
“I didn’t have a period where I studied engineering professionally. Instead, I enrolled in what Japan would call a technical high school that trains technical engineers, and I actually [entered] the electrical department there,” he told me.
Related Story
Robots are bringing new life to extinct species
The field of paleo-inspired robotics is opening up a new way to turn back time and studying prehistoric animals.
Afterward, he worked at Komatsu Manufacturing—because, he said, he liked bulldozers. But in 1974, he saw that Tomy was hiring, and he wanted to make toys. “I was told that it was the No. 1 toy company in Japan, so I decided [it was worth a look],” he said. “I took a night train from Tohoku to Tokyo to take a job exam, and that’s how I ended up joining the company.”
The inspiration for the Armatron came from a newspaper clipping that Watanabe’s boss brought to him one day. “It showed an image of a [mechanical arm] holding an egg with three fingers. I think we started out thinking, ‘This is where things are heading these days, so let’s make this,’” he recalled.
As the lead of a small team, Watanabe briefly turned his attention to another project, and by the time he returned to the robotic arm, the team had a prototype. But it was quite different from the Armatron’s final form. “The hand stuck out from the main body to the side and could only move about 90 degrees. The control panel also had six movement positions, and they were switched using six switches. I personally didn’t like that,” said Watanabe. So he went back to work.
The Armatron’s inventor, Hiroyuki Watanabe, in Tokyo in 2025
COURTESY OF TAKARA TOMY
Watanabe’s breakthrough was inspired by the radio-controlled helicopters he operated as a hobby. Holding up a radio remote controller with dual joystick controls, he told me, “This stick operation allows you to perform four movements with two arms, but I thought that if you twist this part, you can use six movements.”
Watanabe at work at Tomy in Tokyo in 1982.
COURTESY OF HIROYUKI WATANABE
“I had always wanted to create a system that could rotate 360 degrees, so I thought about how to make that system work,” he added.
